title: Two-apart one-sided additive paths compose at recurring lags at every ring size
subject: Paths of rings joined by shared contacts, read with the canonical knot test on their space-time law
conclusion: In paths of four rings of s >= 4 cells with rule 60 or 102 on each ring and the middle rings' contacts two apart, a contact that reads two partners (cells reading only it and themselves) depends on both partners' first values at every lag, so every contact binds both its rings at every lag; and the last contact binds the end rings exactly at the lags T with C(T - 3, m) odd, m = 2, s - 2 or 2s - 6 after mirroring the rule-102 rings. By Lucas' theorem these lags recur with density 2^(-ones in m): each of the 64 families composes at recurring lags with every contact persistent at every ring size, and at every lag at none.
